title: Competence vs competency: what is the difference?
description: Competence is a person's demonstrated ability to achieve intended results; a competency is a defined unit of performance. Why ISO and auditors care.
shortAnswer: Competence is the state of being able to do the work: ISO 9000 defines it as the "ability to apply knowledge and skills to achieve intended results". A competency is a named, defined unit of performance, such as "conducts a risk assessment", listed in a framework and assessed. People have or lack competence; frameworks contain competencies. ISO standards require organizations to ensure and evidence competence, and competencies usually define what that means for each role.
keyTakeaways: Competence describes a person's demonstrated ability to achieve results; a competency describes one defined element of required performance.
ISO management system standards, including ISO 9001 and ISO 45001, use "competence" and require organizations to determine it, ensure it, act on gaps and retain evidence.
HR and workforce systems use "competency" for the items in a framework, often defined as clusters of knowledge, skills and abilities measured against standards.
Auditors test competence, not paperwork: a list of competencies and training records is not evidence that people can achieve intended results.

sections.heading: What is the core difference between competence and competency?

blocks.text: Competence is an attribute of a person in a context: they can or cannot achieve the intended results of their work. A competency is a description written into a framework: a defined piece of performance, with indicators, that people are expected to demonstrate. Competence is the outcome being assured; competencies are the specification used to assure it.

The ISO definition is the anchor for management systems. The ISO 9001 Auditing Practices Group, a joint group of ISO and the International Accreditation Forum (IAF), quotes ISO 9000:2015, 3.10.4: competence is the "ability to apply knowledge and skills to achieve intended results" ([ISO and IAF, Guidance on auditing competence](https://committee.iso.org/files/live/sites/tc176/files/PDF%20APG%20New%20Disclaimer%2012-2023/ISO-TC%20176-TF_APG-Competence.pdf)). The definition is about results, not attendance or qualifications.

Workforce systems define competency as a unit. A US Department of Labor competency model describes a competency as "a cluster of related knowledge, skills, and abilities that affects a major part of one's job (a role or responsibility), that correlates with performance on the job, that can be measured against well-accepted standards, and that can be improved via training and development" ([US Department of Labor](https://www.dol.gov/sites/dolgov/files/ETA/advisories/TEN/2011/ten14_11a1.pdf)). Vocational systems sometimes use the singular in the competence sense: Australia's training package framework, for example, defines competency as "the consistent application of knowledge and skill to the standard of performance required in the workplace" ([DEWR](https://www.dewr.gov.au/download/16680/training-package-organising-framework-effective-1-july-2025/39042/training-package-organising-framework/pdf)).

sections.heading: How do ISO standards use the word competence?

blocks.text: ISO standards use competence for the requirement placed on organizations: determine the competence people need, make sure they have it, act where they do not, and keep evidence. The word appears in clause 7.2 of the harmonized structure shared by ISO management system standards.

items: **ISO 9001 (quality):** clause 7.2 covers people whose work affects quality management system performance. The 2026 edition keeps competence in clause 7.2. See [ISO 9001 competence requirements](/regulations/iso-9001-competence-requirements).

**ISO 45001 (occupational health and safety):** clause 7.2 adds the ability to identify hazards to the competence workers need. See [ISO 45001 competence and awareness](/regulations/iso-45001-competence-and-awareness).

**ISO 10015:2019:** gives guidelines for competence management and people development within quality management, without adding requirements to ISO 9001 ([ISO](https://www.iso.org/standard/69459.html)).

**ISO/IEC 17024 (certification of persons):** schemes certify that individuals are competent for specific tasks. The Irish National Accreditation Board notes that under the standard, competence "can be independent of qualification" ([INAB](https://www.inab.ie/news-resources/publications/iso-iec-17024-conformity-assessment-general-requirements-for-bodies-operating-certification-of-persons.pdf)).

blocks.text: ISO texts do occasionally use "competencies" in the plural, and the Auditing Practices Group guidance makes a point worth quoting: "The qualifications are not always required, but the competencies are." The distinction that matters is between having a qualification and being able to achieve the result.

sections.heading: Why do auditors care about the difference?

blocks.text: Auditors care because a competency list and a training log do not prove competence. Their task is to judge whether the organization determined the competence it needs, provided it, and checked that it worked, so evidence of results carries more weight than evidence of attendance.

The ISO and IAF guidance says an auditor should be able to "assess the process for determining the competences", "observe if competences were appropriately determined", review how actions to achieve them are identified and provided, and review "how evaluation of the effectiveness of those actions is performed". In production and service areas, auditors may observe people against job expectations, interview a sample, confirm they are able to perform their duties, and check whether competent replacements are available when the usual person is absent.

blocks.text: The practical lesson is that a [competency framework](/glossary/competency-framework) is the specification and [competency assessment](/glossary/competency-assessment) is the test. Both are needed to show competence. The comparison of [completion tracking vs competency verification](/compare/completion-tracking-vs-competency-verification) covers the record keeping side.

sections.heading: Which term should an organization use?

blocks.text: Use competence when talking about the requirement and the outcome, especially in management system documents, and competency for the items in your framework. Defining both terms in the framework glossary prevents confusion between HR, quality and compliance teams.

items: In a quality or safety manual: "The organization ensures the competence of persons doing work under its control."
In a role profile: "This role requires the following competencies at practitioner level."
In an assessment record: "Assessed as competent against competency CDD-01 on the date shown, by a qualified assessor."

sections.heading: How does Knowledge Foundry approach this?

blocks.text: Knowledge Foundry links each competency to the obligation it comes from and to the assessment points that evidence it, so an organization can show not only which competencies a role needs but how competence in each was checked. That is the chain auditors follow under clause 7.2.

faqs.q: Is competencies or competences the correct plural?
faqs.a: Both are used. Competences is the plural of competence and is common in European usage, including ESCO and ISO texts. Competencies is the plural of competency and is common in HR and in US and Australian workforce systems. Pick one convention and define it.

faqs.q: Does ISO 9001 require a competency framework?
faqs.a: No. ISO 9001 requires the organization to determine the necessary competence, ensure people are competent, act on gaps, evaluate effectiveness and retain appropriate documented information. A competency framework is a common way to meet the first of these, but the standard does not prescribe its form.

faqs.q: Can someone be competent without a qualification?
faqs.a: Often, yes. Competence is about achieving intended results, and ISO and accreditation guidance note that it can be independent of qualification. Where law or regulation requires a specific qualification or license, that requirement applies in addition to competence.

faqs.q: Are training records evidence of competence?
faqs.a: They are evidence that an action was taken, not that it worked. Auditors look for evaluation of effectiveness, such as assessment results, observation or performance data, alongside training records.
